fatal_errors: The proposed Ti-induced BCC/B2 microstructure is not supported by the cited evidence for the specific NbMoTaW-Ti composition; no evidence establishes that approximately 10 at.% Ti will produce discrete B2 precipitates rather than another phase constitution.
Neither cited source supports improved helium-irradiation tolerance from Ti addition or BCC/B2 interfaces, so the central irradiation mechanism and outcome are speculative.

The hypothesis incorrectly characterizes B2 precipitates as intrinsically ductile and as easing dislocation motion; the cited inverted-microstructure evidence attributes improved ductility primarily to continuity of the ductile BCC matrix and confinement of the generally brittle ordered B2 phase.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the requested balance among room-temperature ductility, elevated-temperature strength, and irradiation tolerance, and it proposes a testable microstructural-engineering alternative. However, it does not reconstruct the target intervention, which was equiatomic Re addition to sputtered nanocrystalline NbMoTaW films followed by room-temperature 120 keV He implantation at 1 × 10^16 ions/cm^2. It also misses the target mediators—grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, amorphous grain-boundary regions, and suppression of grain-boundary He bubbles. The evidence supports inverted BCC+B2 architectures in other refractory alloys and the general NbMoTaW baseline, but not Ti-driven B2 formation or irradiation resistance in NbMoTaW. The proposed experiment has useful controls and measurable endpoints, yet its alloy composition, helium energy, fluence, temperature, and quantitative acceptance thresholds are insufficiently specified, reducing discriminability and making its very broad ambient-to-1600 °C boundary unsupported.
